document.title: GOP Debate: Candidates Clash on Key Issues
document.overview: The first GOP debate since November saw candidates engaging in a free-for-all, focusing on immigration, the Iraq war, abortion, gun control, and the authenticity of the Bible. The debate highlighted personal attacks and policy disagreements among the candidates.
key_findings: Candidates attacked each other on various policy issues, including immigration and the Iraq war.
Romney and Giuliani exchanged accusations about immigration policies.
Huckabee drew cheers for proposing to abolish the IRS.
McCain and Paul had a disagreement over the Iraq war and military spending.
Romney admitted past mistakes on abortion, citing a position from his time as governor of Massachusetts.
technical_details: The debate was the first since a month ago, with five weeks remaining until the first contest of the 2008 nominating season.
CNN and YouTube collaborated to submit video questions to the candidates.
Over 4,000 video submissions were reviewed for the debate, with 2,000 more than the Democratic debate.
implications: The debate showcased the competitive nature of the Republican primary race, with candidates trying to outdo each other in various policy areas.
The event highlighted the need for candidates to be prepared to address a wide range of issues and defend their positions.
The personal nature of some of the attacks suggests the importance of positioning oneself within the party's ideological spectrum.

The debate highlighted contentious exchanges, particularly between Rudy Giuliani and Mitt Romney, regarding illegal immigration policies. The candidates also differed on issues such as tax cuts, gun ownership, and the Iraq war.
key_findings: Candidates engaged in a free-for-all debate, focusing on various contentious issues.
Rudy Giuliani and Mitt Romney had a heated exchange over immigration policies.
John McCain and Ron Paul sparred over the Iraq war, with McCain calling Paul's stance isolationist.
Mitt Romney admitted past mistakes on abortion, stating his previous support for Roe vs. Wade.
Differences in views on tax cuts, gun ownership, and trade with China were highlighted.
